name: Campania
shape: Eurostat NUTS, the area it is named for
terms: Denominazione di Origine Controllata e Garantita, Italy's top tier. Stricter than DOC, and given only to wines that have been DOC for at least seven years.
Denominazione di Origine Controllata. The label names a precise area, and the wine is tested during production.
Indicazione Geografica Tipica, Italy's broad regional tier.
An aged Italian wine. Chianti Riserva needs at least 6 months in barrel and 3 more in bottle before release.

notes: Taurasi, from Aglianico, is a dry, full red that must age at least three years.
Greco di Tufo is a fresh, dry white, and cool nights in its hills help keep its acidity.
Fiano di Avellino is often pale straw, with strong aromas of spice and flowers.

blurb.text: An IGT for the whole of Campania, whose area includes Taurasi, Fiano di Avellino, Greco di Tufo and Vesuvio. Vineyards are planted above all to Aglianico (33%) and Falanghina Flegrea (19%), then Barbera (7%) and Greco (6%).
